answers.answer: Credit Shivam-Fl. That account operates this pipeline, so a person is answerable for every change it ships. Correct both shipped notes to `authors: [Shivam-Fl]`. Then make the release-notes check reject an author that is an agent or a bot, not a person: `claude`, `github-actions`, and anything ending in `[bot]` (case-insensitive). Add a test for each, and a test that `Shivam-Fl` passes. A small denylist is the right rule here; skip the network lookup.

validated_work_order.understanding: The release-notes gate packages/ci-actions/bin/release-notes-check.mjs checks category presence, category membership, authors presence, authors-is-an-array, and a one-line body. It never inspects an author value. I ran the real script on a scratch branch off origin/main whose only new commit added upcoming-release-notes/tmp-bot-author.md with `authors: [claude]`: `BASE_REF=main GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY=/tmp/rn-summary.md node packages/ci-actions/bin/release-notes-check.mjs` printed `Validated 1 release note(s).` and exited 0. That value reaches parseReleaseNotes in src/release-notes/util.mjs, which emits `— thanks @claude` in the published changelog. The issue's proposed handle-shape check cannot catch it: `claude` is a syntactically perfect GitHub handle, and all 39 distinct author values in the directory pass such a rule. The owner's recorded decision is binding and this plan implements it exactly: credit Shivam-Fl on both shipped notes, and reject agents/bots by a small denylist — `claude`, `github-actions`, and anything ending in `[bot]` case-insensitively — with a test per rule plus a test that Shivam-Fl passes, and no network lookup. The plan also re-pins the verification recipes the last review rejected.
validated_work_order.root_cause: validateFile asserts only that `authors` is present and an array; the value of each element is never examined, so any string — a bot login, a first name, a product name — passes the gate that exists to keep the published changelog honest.
validated_work_order.approach: Two halves, one slice. (1) Put the identity rule in a pure, exported, unit-testable helper called from validateFile. It lives in packages/ci-actions/src/release-notes/util.mjs — the existing shared home for release-notes helpers that the check script already imports from — so no new file for one function. The rule is a denylist exactly as decided: lowercase+trim each author, reject if it equals `claude` or `github-actions` or ends in `[bot]` (which already covers `claude[bot]` and `github-actions[bot]`, the logins git history actually shows). The new branch goes after the `Array.isArray(data.authors)` check and before the one-line body check, preserving the existing ordering. (2) Correct the two shipped notes to `authors: [Shivam-Fl]` by editing in place — they are on main. The helper returns the offending values rather than a boolean so the error names what was wrong and what to put instead. No network call: the decision rules it out, and existence on GitHub could not distinguish `claude` (not an account) from `Shivam-Fl` (a real account that asked for the change rather than writing it) anyway. I prototyped the entire change in a throwaway clone of this repository and ran the real gate on it five times: the `claude` note is rejected with `::error::… not bots or agents: claude.` and exit 1; a `Shivam-Fl` note prints `Validated 1 release note(s).` and exits 0; and bad-category, multi-line-body and missing-authors each still fail with their original messages.

files.change: Add an exported `NON_PERSON_AUTHORS` denylist (`['claude', 'github-actions']`) and an exported `findNonPersonAuthors(authors)` that returns the offending entries: lowercase+trim each author, keep it if it is in the denylist or matches /\[bot\]$/. Return an array (empty when every author is a person) rather than a boolean, so the caller can name the bad values in its error. Put it beside `categoryAutocorrections`/`categoryOrder`, which the check script already imports from here. Add a short comment saying why this is a denylist and not a shape check — `claude` is a valid GitHub handle, so only the identity list distinguishes the tool from the person — and that the small size is deliberate, since the network lookup was rejected as slow and token-dependent. Do not touch `parseReleaseNotes` or anything else in this file.
files.why: The check script is a top-level script with side effects (reads env, fetches git, exits) and cannot be imported by a test. util.mjs is the module it already imports for its other two validation constants, so the rule is testable and the diff is one import line.

files.change: In `validateFile`, after the existing `Array.isArray(data.authors)` branch and before the `trimmedContent` check, add: `const nonPersonAuthors = findNonPersonAuthors(data.authors); if (nonPersonAuthors.length > 0) { reportError(`Release note ${path} authors must be GitHub usernames of people, not bots or agents: ${nonPersonAuthors.join(', ')}.`); return false; }`. Add `findNonPersonAuthors` to the existing named import from `../src/release-notes/util.mjs`. Keep the failure message naming the rejected values so the author knows what to replace them with. Change nothing else in this file.
files.why: This is the only place the gate validates `authors`; the composite action that runs it needs no edit, which matters because `.github/**` is a forbidden path.

acceptance.check: End to end: the real gate rejects a note whose only author is 'claude'. Running the check on a scratch branch whose single new commit adds a note with `authors: [claude]` prints `::error::` naming `claude` and exits non-zero, where the same branch printed `Validated 1 release note(s).` and exited 0 before this change.
acceptance.how_to_verify: BASE_REF must be a branch name, never a SHA — the script does `git fetch origin $BASE_REF` then `git diff origin/$BASE_REF...HEAD`, and a raw-SHA fetch creates no refs/remotes/origin/<sha>, so `origin/<sha>` does not resolve and the script dies before validateFile runs. GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY must be exported in every invocation: reportError pipes README.md into `fs.createWriteStream(process.env.GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY)`, which throws ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE when unset. So from a clean checkout at the tip of main: `git checkout -b scratch/rn-check origin/main`; add `upcoming-release-notes/tmp-bot-author.md` with front matter `category: Bugfix` / `authors: [claude]` and a single-line body; commit it as the only new commit (this repo's hooks require the subject to start with `[AI]`); then `BASE_REF=main GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY=/tmp/rn-summary.md node packages/ci-actions/bin/release-notes-check.mjs`. Expect a non-zero exit and `::error::Release note upcoming-release-notes/tmp-bot-author.md authors must be GitHub usernames of people, not bots or agents: claude.` Delete the scratch branch and /tmp/rn-summary.md afterwards. I ran exactly this recipe against a prototype of the change and it produced that output and exit 1; against the unmodified script it printed `Validated 1 release note(s).` and exit 0. (AC-1..AC-5 are the automated coverage; this step proves the wiring from validateFile to the helper, which no unit test reaches.)

qa_script: There is no browser surface here — this is a CI gate and two markdown files. Verify with the shell; do not open http://localhost:3001 looking for it.
`yarn workspace @actual-app/ci-actions test` — all cases green, including the seven new ones in src/release-notes/util.test.js.

Read the diff of packages/ci-actions/src/release-notes/util.mjs: the rule is a lowercase+trim comparison against ['claude', 'github-actions'] plus /\[bot\]$/. Confirm there is no fetch, no API call and no token anywhere in the change, and that parseReleaseNotes is untouched.
Read the diff of packages/ci-actions/bin/release-notes-check.mjs: the new branch sits after the Array.isArray check, returns false, and its error message names the offending values.
`grep -h '^authors:' upcoming-release-notes/*.md | sort -u` — 39 distinct handles, no bot, two Shivam-Fl notes now.

`git diff --stat` — exactly four files: the two notes, the check script, util.mjs, plus the new test. Confirm nothing under `.github/**`, `.sdlc/**`, packages/ci-actions/src/migrations/** or docs/spec/** moved.

The wiring proof (AC-6/AC-8), with the invocation spelled out because getting it wrong produces a confusing failure rather than a clear one. Use BASE_REF=main — a branch name, never a SHA: the script resolves origin/$BASE_REF and a parent-SHA fetch creates no such ref, so `git diff origin/<sha>...HEAD` fails with 'ambiguous argument' before any validation runs. And export GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY every time, including the run expected to succeed: reportError pipes README.md into fs.createWriteStream(process.env.GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY), which throws ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE when unset. Sequence: `git checkout -b scratch/rn-check origin/main`; write upcoming-release-notes/tmp-bot-author.md with `category: Bugfix`, `authors: [claude]`, one-line body; commit (subject must start with `[AI]` for this repo's hooks); run `BASE_REF=main GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY=/tmp/rn-summary.md node packages/ci-actions/bin/release-notes-check.mjs` — expect non-zero exit and `::error::` naming `claude`; then edit the note to `authors: [Shivam-Fl]`, commit, run the identical command — expect `Validated 1 release note(s).` and exit 0. Finally `git checkout main && git branch -D scratch/rn-check` and remove /tmp/rn-summary.md.
risks: The denylist is a denylist: `copilot`, `cursor-agent`, `codex` or any future agent login still passes. The owner chose this explicitly over a network lookup, so it is a decision to carry, not a gap to route around — say so in the code comment so the next person does not mistake it for an oversight.

A false positive would block a real contributor: someone whose actual GitHub handle is `claude` or `github-actions` can no longer be credited. No such account appears in the 39 distinct author values in the directory, and the error names the value so it is diagnosable, but the failure mode is a red CI on an honest PR.
`validateFile` reports the first failing note and returns; the new branch follows that existing pattern rather than accumulating errors, so a PR with two bad notes is told about one at a time.
No new host is contacted. The change makes no network call of any kind, so nothing is added to env.api_allowlist in .sdlc/config.yml and QA is not blocked on an allowlist entry.

No forbidden path is touched. `.github/actions/release-notes/check/action.yml` needs no edit — it invokes `node packages/ci-actions/bin/release-notes-check.mjs` and reads the exit code — which matters because `.github/**` is in forbidden_paths.

Note that the composite check action has no caller in this repository's own workflows (`grep -rn 'release-notes/check' .github/` returns nothing), so the gate runs on upstream Actual, not here. The fix is still correct and still ships; it just will not be exercised by this repo's CI until something wires the action up. Wiring it is out of scope.

The verification recipes depend on the script's BASE_REF contract staying as it is — a remote-tracking ref. If that ever changes to accept a SHA, the recipes keep working as written only because `main` is a branch; that is the more robust spelling either way, so keep it.
out_of_scope: Making the check action run in this repository's CI — it has no caller in .github/workflows/ today, and adding one means editing .github/**, a forbidden path.
The shape check the issue originally proposed. It is subsumed and was shown not to catch the reported bug: `claude` is a valid handle shape, so the rule passes both shipped notes unchanged.

Correcting the shape of the two notes' git authorship — both fixes were committed by github-actions[bot] and carry no human review. Decided: Shivam-Fl is credited and the pipeline does not rewrite history.
Any other release-notes field. `category` and the one-line body are validated as they were; nothing else in the front matter is checked and nothing else is added.

Validating authors in release-notes-generate.mjs, which renders `@<author>` into the published changelog. The gate is the correct seam — it fails the PR before it merges rather than at release time — and the generator's own blog `authors:` comes from GITHUB_ACTOR, not from these files.
validated_work_order.confidence_rationale: Higher than the rejected plan because the change itself has now been executed end to end rather than described: I prototyped the helper and the validateFile branch in a throwaway clone and ran the real gate five times — `authors: [claude]` is rejected with `::error::… not bots or agents: claude.` and exit 1, `authors: [Shivam-Fl]` prints `Validated 1 release note(s).` with exit 0, and the bad-category, multi-line-body and missing-authors cases each still fail with their original messages. The rejection's two mechanical claims are also reproduced rather than assumed: `git fetch origin <sha>` leaves no remote-tracking ref and `git rev-parse origin/<sha>` fails with 'ambiguous argument', while `git fetch origin main` creates refs/remotes/origin/main; and fs.createWriteStream(undefined) throws ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE, which is what reportError hits when GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY is unset. Every recipe is now pinned to BASE_REF=main with GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY exported. The residual uncertainty is not about correctness: there is no browser surface, so every criterion is verified with `verify: "test"` and a named command, and the composite action is not wired into any workflow in this repository, so CI here will not exercise the new branch.
evidence: Reproduced the defect with the re-pinned invocation, in a throwaway clone of this repository with a bare repo as origin: on a scratch branch off origin/main whose single new commit adds upcoming-release-notes/tmp-bot-author.md with `authors: [claude]`, `BASE_REF=main GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY=/tmp/rn-summary.md node packages/ci-actions/bin/release-notes-check.mjs` printed `Looking in …` then `Validated 1 release note(s).` and exited 0.

Confirmed the rejected recipe's git failure is real. In a scratch repo: after `git fetch origin <parent-sha>`, `git for-each-ref refs/remotes` prints nothing (only FETCH_HEAD is written) and `git rev-parse origin/<parent-sha>` fails with `fatal: ambiguous argument 'origin/<parent-sha>': unknown revision or path not in the working tree`, as does `git diff origin/<parent-sha>...HEAD`. After `git fetch origin trunk` instead, refs/remotes/origin/trunk exists and `git rev-parse origin/trunk` resolves. So the previous AC-6/AC-8/qa_script recipe died before validateFile ran.

Confirmed the GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY claim: `node -e "fs.createWriteStream(undefined)"` throws `ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE — The "path" argument must be of type string…`, which is exactly what reportError hits at release-notes-check.mjs:30-31 when the variable is unset.

Ran the prototype fix end to end with the corrected recipe. With `authors: [claude]`: exit 1 and `::error::Release note upcoming-release-notes/tmp-bot-author.md authors must be GitHub usernames of people, not bots or agents: claude.` With `authors: [Shivam-Fl]`: `Validated 1 release note(s).`, exit 0. With `category: Nonsense`: the original category error, exit 1. With a two-line body: the original one-line-body error, exit 1. With no `authors:` key: the original missing-authors error, exit 1. The rest of the gate is untouched by the new branch.

Sanity-checked the helper directly against the seven planned cases: `[]`, `['claude']`, `['github-actions']`, `['dependabot[bot]','some-bot[BOT]','claude[bot]']`, `['claude','github-actions']` for the mixed list, `[]` for an empty array — every one matches the expected value.

Read packages/ci-actions/bin/release-notes-check.mjs: `validateFile` contains exactly four checks — data.category present, category in categoryOrder (after categoryAutocorrections), data.authors present, Array.isArray(data.authors), then the one-line body. No check reads an element of data.authors. The fix inserts the authors check between the array check and the body check.

Confirmed the shape rule does not catch it: `grep -h '^authors:' upcoming-release-notes/*.md | sort -u` yields 39 distinct handles across 83 files, all syntactically valid GitHub handles including the two bad ones. There is nothing to shape-reject.

Confirmed the downstream damage: packages/ci-actions/src/release-notes/util.mjs line ~36 does `data.authors.map(a => `@${a}`)` and builds `- ${prefix}${body.trim()} — thanks ${authors}`, so `authors: [claude]` ships to users as `— thanks @claude`.

Confirmed blast radius is exactly two files: `grep -ln '^authors:.*\(claude\|github-actions\|\[bot\]\)' upcoming-release-notes/*.md` returns fix-invalid-regex-rule-crash.md and fix-weekly-report-final-bucket.md. The other notes carry real handles.

Confirmed the test file will be collected: packages/ci-actions/vitest.config.mts sets `include: ['src/**/*.test.(js|jsx|ts|tsx)']`, and the sibling src/build-runs/resolve.test.js is `.js` importing a `.mjs` module — the same shape as the planned util.test.js.

Confirmed the constraint that matters: `grep -rn 'release-notes/check' .github/` returns nothing, so no workflow in this repository invokes the composite action; and .github/actions/release-notes/check/action.yml runs the script directly (`node packages/ci-actions/bin/release-notes-check.mjs`) with `BASE_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.ref }}` — a branch name, which is why the re-pinned recipes use one. It needs no edit.

alternatives_considered.approach: Validate the GitHub handle shape (alphanumerics and single hyphens, no spaces), as the issue text proposed.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It does not catch the bug it was filed for. I ran it over all 39 distinct author values in the directory: zero fail, including both `claude` entries, because `claude` is a syntactically perfect handle. It would have let the next `authors: [claude]` through unchanged. The owner's decision replaces it with an identity denylist.

alternatives_considered.approach: Call the GitHub API to confirm each author exists.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Decided against by the owner, and it would not work anyway: `claude` is not an account, but `Shivam-Fl` is a real account that asked for the change rather than writing it, so existence cannot distinguish the tool from the person. It would also make a fast gate slow and token-dependent.

alternatives_considered.approach: Ship only the two file corrections and leave the gate alone.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: This is what the previous plan stage asked about and the owner answered: a hand-corrected note leaves nothing stopping the third one. The recurrence path is the gate, so the gate is the fix.

alternatives_considered.approach: Put the rule in a new packages/ci-actions/src/release-notes/authors.mjs alongside util.mjs.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: One function, one caller, in a directory where util.mjs is already the shared home for release-notes helpers and is already imported by the very script that needs this. A new module would be an abstraction with one caller; exporting from util.mjs is a two-line diff.

alternatives_considered.approach: Return a boolean from the helper and let the check script write its own message.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The gate would then say an author is invalid without saying which one. The values are already in hand at the point of failure; returning them costs nothing and makes the error actionable, which is the entire point of the ticket.

alternatives_considered.approach: Pass BASE_REF as the parent commit SHA in the verification recipes, as the previous plan did.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Rejected by the plan review, and I reproduced the failure: the script resolves `origin/$BASE_REF`, a raw-SHA fetch writes only FETCH_HEAD and no refs/remotes/origin/<sha>, so `git diff` aborts with 'ambiguous argument' before validateFile ever runs. A correct PR would have failed QA. All recipes now use BASE_REF=main, matching what the composite action passes in production.

alternatives_considered.approach: Make reportError tolerate an unset GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY so the recipes can omit it.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It would mean editing the gate's error path to accommodate the test harness. Exporting one environment variable in the recipe is the smaller change and leaves the production code as it is; the recipe now exports it on every invocation, including the runs expected to succeed.

assumptions: The owner's answer to `/sdlc answer` is binding and is implemented exactly: both notes become `authors: [Shivam-Fl]`, and the denylist is `claude`, `github-actions`, and anything ending in `[bot]` case-insensitively, with no network lookup. I agree with it and found no reason to deviate.

"Anything ending in [bot]" is read case-insensitively because the decision says so; lowercasing the value before both the equality test and the regex covers `CLAUDE`, `Github-Actions` and `SomeBot[BOT]` alike. This is strictly stronger than testing the bare names case-sensitively and cannot reject a real contributor who happens to capitalise differently.

The test file is `util.test.js` rather than `.ts`. The module under test is `util.mjs`, which is plain JavaScript with no types, and the sibling `src/build-runs/resolve.test.js` is `.js` for the same reason. The vitest include glob is `src/**/*.test.(js|jsx|ts|tsx)`, so `.js` is collected.

The verification recipes run in a scratch branch created from `origin/main`, with the temporary note committed as the only new commit. That mirrors the composite action, which passes the pull request's base branch name as BASE_REF and diffs it against HEAD. The recipes name `main` because that is this repository's default branch; on a fork with a different default, substitute it.
The seven unit cases plus the two file corrections are the whole change. No interface surface exists to plan: this is a CI script and two markdown files, with no screen, no API and no state.
unknowns: Whether the owner wants the composite action wired into this repository's own CI. Nothing under .github/workflows/ calls .github/actions/release-notes/check today, so the fix will not be exercised here — and wiring it means touching .github/**, which no agent may do. Left out of scope and named in risks; a human can decide.
Whether the upstream Actual project wants the same denylist. This change lands in Shivam-Fl's fork; whether it is proposed upstream is a human's call, not this ticket's.
residual_risks: Only `claude` and `github-actions` are denied by name. A note crediting `copilot`, `cursor-agent`, `codex` or a future agent login still passes the gate. Carried deliberately, per the decision; a human who wants it closed needs a different rule.
The gate's reach is upstream, not this repository — see the unknown above. The unit tests plus the AC-6/AC-8 manual recipe are the only proof in this repo that the rule works.

Correcting the notes does not change what was already published. If a release already shipped `— thanks @claude`, that text is in the git history of the blog post and in readers' release notes; this change prevents the recurrence, it does not retract the past.
